audit.whatIsWrong: Row 1 read 'Volibear' and row 6 read 'Skill' in both layers; the packet chart gives Skill and Warwick. The content whys already said 'Level 2 stays skill' and 'the late edge is Warwick's', so both rows printed a token contradicting the sentence beside it.
audit.why: At level 2 Jaws of the Beast (8/7.5/7/6.5/6s) heals him for the damage it deals, which cancels out a two-bite Frenzied Maul trade before you have W ranks. Late, Eternal Hunger heals him for his bonus magic damage below 50% health and triples that below 25%, while Blood Hunt (80/70/60/50/40s) gives move and attack speed toward anyone under those thresholds — he wins drawn-out fights you cannot disengage from.
audit.corrected: phases[1]/win[1] set to Skill and phases[6]/win[6] set to Warwick as one atomic group, ratings moved to 5/10 and 4/10, and both whys rewritten to stop claiming a Volibear win.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[6].why claimed Volibear is a drain-tank Warwick cannot burst at two items, which is backwards — that is the stage Warwick takes.
audit.why: Warwick's scaling is the opposite of burst: Eternal Hunger's healing triples below 25% health and Blood Hunt tracks and speeds him toward low targets, so the longer a late fight runs the further ahead he gets. The right instruction is to close the game on the mid-game lead, which content late already says.
audit.corrected: phases[6].why now names Eternal Hunger's below-25% triple heal and Blood Hunt, and tells you to end early.

audit.whatIsWrong: The matchup's single best interaction is stated with the wrong ability in four places: whys[4], spikes[1].text, wants.you[1] and content.mid all say 'E-stun' cancels Infinite Duress.
audit.why: Sky Splitter (E, 16s) damages, slows and shields Volibear when he stands in the blast — it has no stun at all, so a player following this advice presses a button that does not interrupt anything and gets suppressed for 1.5s. Thundering Smash (Q, 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s) is the stun, and Infinite Duress is a channel, so hard CC is what breaks it. The Q is also an auto-attack reset, so the stun lands on the next attack — hold it for his leap rather than spending it on the walk-up.
audit.corrected: All four fields now name the Q stun, and spikes[1].text states outright that Infinite Duress is a channel and that the Q is held for his leap.

audit.whatIsWrong: packet.defects flags zero cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere on the page — no 'wait for X before you Y' line carried a number.
audit.why: The two numbers that decide this lane are Jaws of the Beast at 8s rank 1 (his sustain refresh) and Infinite Duress at 110/90/70s (the thing you hold Q for). Without them the advice 'trade around his cooldowns' is unactionable.
audit.corrected: phases[1].why now carries the 8s rank-1 Q heal cooldown; spikes[1].text keys the Q stun explicitly to his leap.

edits.before: Q + W online — stun in, double-bite out. Warwick has to respect every walk-up once your second W heal-bite threatens.
edits.after: Q + W online, but Jaws of the Beast (8s at rank 1) heals him for what you take, so trades cancel out until you rank W up.

edits.before: With two items you're a drain-tank Warwick can't burst. Only discipline beats you now — never int the Q stun into ready CC and the lane stays yours.
edits.after: Two items in he out-scales you: Eternal Hunger triples its healing below 25% health and Blood Hunt drags him onto you, so end the game early.

edits.before: Level 6 is yours: E-stun cancels Infinite Duress and Stormbringer wins the all-in.
edits.after: Level 6 is yours: the Q stun cancels Infinite Duress and Stormbringer wins the all-in.

edits.before: Both ult: your Stormbringer dive and CC beat his Infinite Duress suppress if you E-stun him mid-channel or before he leaps.
edits.after: Both ult: Infinite Duress is a channel, so Thundering Smash's stun breaks it — hold the Q for his leap, not for the walk-up.

edits.before: From 3 through first item you take over — Frenzied Maul stacking and passive attack speed out-sustain his Q heal, and your E stun answers his level-6 Infinite Duress.
edits.after: From 3 through first item you take over — Frenzied Maul stacking and passive attack speed out-sustain his Q heal, and your Q stun answers his level-6 Infinite Duress.

notes: The 'E-stun cancels Infinite Duress' line was repeated in four fields and is the most dangerous error on this page: Sky Splitter has no stun, so the player presses E, nothing is interrupted, and he eats a 1.5s suppression. Thundering Smash is the stun and Infinite Duress is a channel, so the interaction is real — it just needs the right key. Chart rows 1 and 6 realigned to the packet in both layers. Whether tenacity meaningfully shortens Primal Howl's 1s flee, and whether the flee can be cleansed, are not in Riot's text and I asserted neither.
